$comment: Extractor INPUT contract (WS-13 §3/§13; OmniRoute report §11.2). Hand-maintained and reviewed, in two halves. (1) `paths` is the VERSIONED path allowlist the sparse checkout materializes — the extractor refuses to materialize anything outside it and never widens the boundary on its own. (2) `providers` is the reviewed provider intake list: a row's `risk` is what the extractor stamps onto the generated WinterProviderDescriptor, and promoting one to "approved" is a deliberate, reviewed edit. No upstream source is vendored under this directory beyond the upstream LICENSE/NOTICE copies the extraction manifest records — see README.md.

importBoundary.$comment: WS-13 §3 step 2 says an import outside the allowlist "fails the job for review; the boundary never auto-widens". Taken as a rule about WIDENING, not about aborting: the literal extractor never follows an import at all, so a value that would have to come from an unmaterialized module is DROPPED with a recorded rejection (`unresolved-reference`), and the offending specifier is listed in the ledger's `outOfAllowlistImports` so drift stays visible. Aborting instead would make the pipeline unrunnable by construction — `open-sse/config/providers/shared.ts` imports a dozen modules outside any reviewable provider-data boundary. The boundary keeps its teeth through `failOnUnresolvedFields`: an allowlisted provider whose IDENTITY-critical field cannot be resolved from materialized files fails the run for review.

modelOverrides.$comment: ONE hand-reviewed per-model override map, applied by the mapper and RECORDED in the ledger as a `reviewed-normalization` — never a heuristic, and never silent. Three narrow things it can say about a single upstream model id: `id` corrects a wire id upstream spells differently from the provider's own documentation; `exclude` keeps a row out of the catalog entirely (WS-13 §4's MUST that non-`llm` rows never reach the worker-model picker — upstream has no per-model scope field, and a NAME heuristic would be worse than none because it would silently drop a future model whose id happens to match); `status` overrides the provider's `initialModelStatus` for one row. Every entry carries a `why` that ends up in the ledger, so a reviewer can diff the catalog against the pinned source and find every place they differ with the justification attached.

auto.why: OpenRouter documents its auto-router as the qualified id `openrouter/auto`; the pinned upstream entry lists a bare `{ id: "auto" }`. Keeping upstream's spelling put `auto` on the wire from BOTH resolution paths — step 1 (the seeded row's own upstreamId) and the `allowUnlisted` pass-through, which strips a self-prefix. Correcting it here fixes both at once, and the `auto` alias keeps the bare spelling resolvable.
